headings.leadersBlurb: These four are the automatic NFC seeds. Everyone else is chasing the three wild cards.
headings.pathsBlurb: Win the NFC South, or be one of the three best remaining clubs in the conference. The closer route is the one that matters.
headings.footer: Updated from ESPN’s public NFL feeds. Not affiliated with the NFL, the Atlanta Falcons, or ESPN.
headings.footerTiny: Seven NFC teams qualify: four division winners and three wild cards. The playoff percentage is a season simulation from point differential and home field. It is not a betting line.
headings.conclusion: The Atlanta Falcons have been mathematically eliminated from the NFL playoffs.
headings.injuryBlurb: Falcons listed as injured or on injured reserve. A Tuesday practice note can move before Sunday.
headings.rootingBlurb: Who needs to lose for the division or the cut line to get closer. Not a betting line, and not a live in-game number.

narrative.headline: A half-game back of the South
narrative.blurb: The Falcons are 3-6 with a -35 point differential, a half-game behind the Buccaneers in the NFC South, and two and a half games off the last wild-card berth. 8 games left, starting Sunday at home against the Chiefs.

division.title: NFC South
division.detail: The Buccaneers lead at 3-5. The Falcons are 1-2 inside the division. Win the South and the seed is automatic.

wildcard.title: Wild card
wildcard.detail: The Packers hold the last berth at 5-3. Three wild cards get in after the four division winners.

tableBlurb: Seven NFC clubs play on: four division winners and three wild cards. The line under the seventh seed is the whole race.

tiebreak.headToHead: Head-to-head inside the South: L 3–34 vs CAR; W 45–24 @ NO; L 0–16 @ TB.
tiebreak.detail: If the South finishes level, the NFL starts with head-to-head, then division record, then common games, then conference record. Point differential is the eye test. It is not the first tiebreaker.
